title: Kalki
tomorrow: after Kalki, what's the first sign that a new age has begun?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kalki: the one name in the series still written as will be, an event ahead for some readers and a promise for others. Today, the age he's promised to.

Scroll any comment section long enough and the complaints start to rhyme: money buys respect, the loudest one wins, a costume passes for the real thing. Here's an older version. Wealth will count as good birth. Might will decide what's just. A thread worn on the body will be enough to call someone a Brahmin. Being clever with words will pass for learning. It sounds like today because it's built from the same complaint. It's the Bhagavata Purana, forecasting the age Kalki is born into.
screen: `THE COMPLAINTS START TO RHYME.` → `WEALTH FOR BIRTH. MIGHT FOR RIGHT.` → `A FORECAST, NOT A FEED.`

segments.voice: The Bhagavata's last book opens like this: day by day, under the force of time, truthfulness, mercy and patience will wear thin, and even strength and memory with them. Then comes that list. Notice what it's really about. Not monsters or floods. Stand-ins: money standing in for good character, a thread standing in for a Brahmin's life, smooth talk standing in for learning, strength standing in for justice. The Kali age, as the Bhagavata draws it, is an age of substitutes. One thing to hear clearly: Kali, the age, isn't Kālī, the goddess. They're two different Sanskrit words, with short vowels for the age and long ones for the goddess. And now the turn, and it's a sound. The same book, after all that gloom, says the Kali age is an ocean of faults with one great good: simply by singing Krishna's name, a person can be set free. That singing is kirtan, sometimes one voice leading a line and a whole room answering it. In an age of stand-ins, the Bhagavata points to something plain: a voice, saying a name, again and again.
screen: `TRUTH, MERCY, PATIENCE WEAR THIN.` · `AN AGE OF STAND-INS.` · `KALI THE AGE, KALI THE GODDESS: TWO WORDS.` · `ONE GREAT GOOD: SINGING THE NAME.` · then, large: `A HARD AGE, ONE DOOR OPEN.`

segments.voice: Choose one word that matters to you, a name of God if you pray, or a word like peace if you don't, and say it softly on each breath out. Keep your voice low and even, the way a room answers a leader's line. For the last part of the sit, just listen to the quiet after it.
Kalki: promised in the Bhagavata to the Kali age, an age of stand-ins with one door left open.
Your line: Kalki. Promised to a hard age, and the age still has an open door. More tomorrow.

Kali.meaning: the dark age, the last in the Bhagavata's cycle

Kālī.meaning: a goddess; her name is a different word from the age

Brahmin.meaning: a member of the priestly class
